body: SHOULD-FIX (comment law; needs a coordinator ruling on the number). Five has no stated basis and the comment above it cites eight. The ticket's seven of eleven wrong under the old rule means about two thirds of calls landed off the holder; at that rate five reads with one re-ask still let roughly one delete in eight to one in five say gone wrongly (rough, eleven samples, independence assumed). Eight reads: about one in thirty to one in fifteen. Twelve: one in sixty or better, at about 0.3 s a read. Extra asks are the other lever, since a DELETE on a gone machine is harmless on both providers. Whatever number is ruled, one clause here should say why it is enough. Full arithmetic in the review body.

NIT (test discipline). This passes with the at-once re-ask replaced by a streak reset, because the grace-window second attempt also reaches two deletes; only the Box test pins the re-ask at once. Asserting that the second DELETE is the call right after the running read would make the title true of this test alone.

Fixed in d4454a3df (now in ed1c50670, merged with main at 9635c3e87): `GONE_READS = 12` and `KILL_ASKS = 3` per the coordinator ruling on wsp-map#1235, and the comment gives the measured skew and the one-in-sixty clause. The failure lines now say three asks and three kills.

Fixed in d4454a3df (now in ed1c50670, head 9635c3e87): the test runs with a 60 s grace window and asserts DELETE, GET, GET, DELETE, then `GONE_READS` GETs after the create. With the break replaced by a streak reset, it times out.
